rationale: The agent authenticated the user by matching full name and zip to a single account via tools, then retrieved the user and order details before taking action. The agent sought explicit confirmation before attempting any order modification and again before updating the default address. When the modify tool revealed that partial cancellations weren’t supported (exchange-only), the agent correctly explained the limitation and offered viable alternatives. The user chose to keep the order and update the default address; the agent confirmed the exact Seattle address and, after user approval, successfully updated it with the modify_user_address tool and reported the correct final state. No writes were performed without confirmation, no actions were taken on the wrong account, and final information (address update) matched the tool results. While the agent mentioned order statuses and refund timing without explicit tool evidence shown in the transcript, these did not lead to incorrect actions or misinformation in the final outcome, and the partial-cancel attempt was properly handled based on tool errors. Overall, the user’s request (given tool constraints) was completed in line with policy.
